Run one replicate of CATE estimators

Source: R/sim-cate-run.R
sim_cate_one_rep.Rd

Draws one dataset from the named DGP (via sim_cate_data()), then runs each requested method on the same dataset and returns per-replicate performance metrics aligned with the paper's evaluation criteria.

Usage

sim_cate_one_rep(
  n,
  kx,
  k,
  s,
  design,
  methods = "dnn_oracle",
  tuning = NULL,
  tuning_mode = c("default", "grid"),
  alpha = 0.05,
  seed = NULL,
  sigma = 0.5,
  clip = 0.001,
  n_folds = 5L
)

Arguments

n

Integer sample size.

kx

Integer covariate dimension (\(\ge 2\)).

k

Integer DNN neighbour count.

s

Integer kernel order (undersmoothing parameter). May be omitted when tuning is supplied.

design

Character DGP name; passed to sim_cate_data().

methods

Character vector of method names; see sim_cate_methods(). Default: "dnn_oracle".

tuning

Optional kernel-order tuning specification.

tuning_mode

One of "default" or "grid". "default" evaluates one scalar kernel order. "grid" requires tuning and emits one row per DNN candidate while non-DNN benchmarks remain one row per replicate.

alpha

Nominal coverage level (default 0.05).

seed

Optional integer seed for this replicate.

sigma

Noise SD forwarded to the DGP.

clip

Propensity clipping bound forwarded to the DGP and cross-fitting.

n_folds

Number of cross-fitting folds for the dnn_crossfit method.

Value

A data.frame with one or more rows per method and columns method, candidate_id, lambda, s, tau_hat, tau0, bias, sq_err, se, cover (0/1), ci_len, neff, and status. Methods based on GRF also record method_variant, forest_nuisance, and whether Y.hat and W.hat were supplied. The maintained causal_forest route uses externally supplied oracle nuisance inputs. with explicit localization weights also report the realized DNN-weighted truth, realized localization drift, estimator remainder, studentized error, physical 90-percent-mass radius, treatment-arm effective sample sizes, and the top-five score-contribution share. The localized_truth field is the finite-sample object \(\sum_i W_{i,s}(x_0)\tau_0(X_i)\), not the deterministic population branch. With \(x_0\) and \((n,s)\) fixed, expectation over the i.i.d. covariate sample and complete-DNN exchangeability give $$E(\mathrm{localized\_truth})=\alpha_s(x_0).$$ The historical branch_drift field name is retained for compatibility; it stores realized localization drift. The estimator remainder combines centered score variation with fitted-state effects. Failed methods have NA for all metric columns and status = "failed"; registered route metadata is retained when it is known from the selected method.

Examples

rep1 <- sim_cate_one_rep(
  n = 200, kx = 2, k = 1, s = 12,
  design = "dgp2_nonlinear",
  methods = c("dnn_fullsample", "ols_interact"),
  seed = 1
)
rep1
